newsitem.title: USA: TIG stock tumbles on disappointing earnings and warning.
newsitem.headline: TIG stock tumbles on disappointing earnings and warning.

text.p: The stock of TIG Holdings Inc. lost more than 11 percent of its value Monday after the insurance company reported disappointing earnings for the first quarter and warned about the outlook for earnings growth.
TIG tumbled $3.50 to $27.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The New York-based property and casualty insurance firm said it earned $36.4 million, or 63 cents a share, in the first three months of the year, compared with a loss of $30.8 million, or 53 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenues fell to $428.6 million from $455.4 million.
The earnings were short of Wall Street's estimates of 68 cents a share.
Last year's loss stemmed from the company's decision to take charges of up to $100 million to restructure its commercial insurance operations.
TIG said non-catastrophe property losses in its retail and commercial speciality divisions eroded its first quarter results.
"We are in the process of refining our retail business strategy to reduce the exposure to and the impact from these types of losses," said Jon Rotenstreich, chairman and chief executive oficer.
In addition, he said, competitive market conditions in the commercial insurance and reinsurance industry have encouraged TIG to remain selective in its underwriting process.
"We do not anticipate any change in pricing conditions during 1997. Therefore, these conditions could moderate earnings growth until our recent initiatives reach full production," he said.
